actor_types.label: leader or founder
actor_types.definition: Leads, directs, chairs, founded or sits on the board of an organisation, ministry or campaign.

actor_types.label: therapist or counsellor
actor_types.definition: Psychotherapist, psychologist, counsellor, coach or other practitioner offering talking therapy or guidance.

actor_types.label: pastor or clergy
actor_types.definition: Holds a religious office: pastor, priest, minister, elder, imam, rabbi.

actor_types.label: went through change efforts
actor_types.definition: Says, or is said, to have gone through change efforts, including people who call themselves ex-gay or ex-trans, whether they now speak for or against them.

actor_types.label: researcher
actor_types.definition: Academic, scientist, theologian or ethicist writing as a scholar, or the author of a study.

actor_types.label: medical professional
actor_types.definition: Doctor, psychiatrist, nurse or other health professional.

actor_types.label: politician or legislator
actor_types.definition: Member of a parliament, minister, rapporteur or elected official.

actor_types.label: journalist
actor_types.definition: Reporter, editor, interviewer or presenter for a news outlet or programme.

actor_types.label: activist or campaigner
actor_types.definition: Campaigns for or against change efforts or a ban, without a leading role in an organisation.

actor_types.label: family member
actor_types.definition: Parent, spouse or relative speaking as such.

actor_types.label: ministry
actor_types.definition: Religious ministry, outreach or support group offering help with sexuality or gender.

actor_types.label: therapy practice
actor_types.definition: Clinic, practice or company offering therapy, counselling or coaching.

actor_types.label: church or religious body
actor_types.definition: Church, denomination, parish, mosque, religious order or federation.

actor_types.label: advocacy group
actor_types.definition: Campaign, charity or non-governmental organisation working for a cause.

actor_types.label: professional body
actor_types.definition: Association or regulator of a profession (counsellors, psychologists, doctors).

actor_types.label: media outlet
actor_types.definition: Newspaper, broadcaster, magazine, news site or channel.

actor_types.label: government or parliament
actor_types.definition: Government, ministry, parliament, committee, court or public agency.

actor_types.label: political party
actor_types.definition: Political party or its group in a parliament.

function_definitions.Slur: A word used to insult LGBTQ+ people as a group or a person.
function_definitions.Euphemism: A softer word that hides what a practice is or does ("journey", "wholeness", "unwanted attraction", "exploration").
function_definitions.Conspiracy: Words that cast LGBTQ+ people, rights or institutions as a hidden, coordinated plot.
function_definitions.Pseudo-Diagnostic: A made-up or discredited diagnosis or cause presented as clinical fact ("father wound", "gender confusion disorder").
function_definitions.Identity-Policing: Words that tell people how they may or may not name or express themselves ("don't call yourself gay").
function_definitions.Moral-Purity Frame: Words that cast sexuality or gender in terms of purity, sin, holiness or cleanness.
function_definitions.Political Slogan: A catchphrase used in a campaign ("protect our children", "let us pray").
function_definitions.Recruitment Frame: Words that address the reader as someone who needs change ("Are you struggling with same-sex attraction?").
function_definitions.Pastoral Rhetoric: Caring, spiritual language that presents change efforts as love or help ("walk alongside", "freedom in Christ").
function_definitions.Promotional Recruitment: A call to join, enrol, book, donate or get in touch with a programme or ministry.
function_definitions.Testimonial Marketing: A personal story of change used to promote a programme, ministry or therapy.
function_definitions.Disinformation Narrative: Not offered to the taggers: calling a narrative false is a ruling on truth, which the archive does not make (claims are attributed, never ruled true or false).
